v.why: An input-to-output identity shortcut adds more when the other path into the output is a deep conv chain that benefits from a short gradient route.
Two stacked average pools on 0->2->3 low-pass the small images twice and erase detail, so the second pool hurts more.
Pooling learned conv features gives useful local invariance, whereas pooling raw-input copies only blurs.
With an identity shortcut already reaching the output, an extra deep conv on 1->2 adds mostly overfitting capacity and little validation gain.
A skip on 0->2 parallel to a conv series path 0->1->2 forms a residual block, which helps most when the branch is a deep nonlinear conv.
With edge 5 removed, edge 4 is the only route from node 1 and node 2 to the output, so its capacity is scarcer and upgrading it matters more.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 receives no signal and edge 4 is a dead path, so the upgrade has almost no effect.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is empty and edge 2 carries nothing, so the edit cannot help.
Without edge 4, edge 0's features reach the output only via the longer 1->2->3 route, which limits its influence.
Upgrading a 1x1 conv to 3x3 is a smaller change than replacing none, skip or pool, so its gain is below average.
Adding a conv where the direct input-to-output edge was absent creates a new path and gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv reconnects node 2 to the output, which gains more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv opens a new route from node 1 to the output, which gains more than replacing another op.
A 3x3 conv already feeding the output sum from the input makes another 3x3 conv from node 1 partly redundant, so gains saturate.
With a strong 3x3 conv already supplying the output, an additional conv on 2->3 adds diminishing capacity.
Adding an identity shortcut where no direct edge existed gives a new short path and gains more than replacing a conv, pool or other op.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv adds a new parallel route into node 2, which gains more than swapping an existing op.
Replacing none with a 3x3 conv creates the deeper 0->1->2 route, which gains more than replacing an existing op.
Replacing none on the first edge reconnects node 1 and downstream edges to the input, which gains far more than replacing another op.
When node 1 already feeds the output through a 3x3 conv, a parallel 3x3 conv from the input is largely redundant.

- The edge 0 and edge 1 redundancy claims with an edge 0 skip.
